body:
Point 1 ~~> 13.3.2 Verify that access to secret assets adheres to the principle of least privilege.~~ ~~Just a duplication of authorization requirements? Maybe mentioning in section text is enough?~~ edit: as it (most likely) is not part of the application authorization flow, it requires a separate requirement. The same way we have separate requirement for logs: 16.4.2 --- Point 2 > 13.3.3 Verify that key material is not exposed to the application (neither the frontend nor the backend) but instead uses an isolated security module like a vault for cryptographic operations. Reword it to positive requirement? ---
Point 3 - spin-off to #2971

> 13.3.4 Verify that key secrets have defined expiration dates and are rotated on a schedule based on the organization's threat model and business requirements. Should the second part have matching documentation requirement?

comments.body:
Agreed 13.3.2 can go away. The point was that setting up proper roles and similar for secrets is super fundamental to secrets management lifecycle. It so often done wrong, I think adding this to the section text is a good idea. But I can see why you would want it to go away.

For 13.3.3, how about:

_13.3.3 Verify that all cryptographic operations are performed using an isolated security module (such as a vault or hardware security module) to securely manage and protect key material from exposure to both frontend and backend components._

For 13.3.4:

Having a matching documentation requirement for 13.3.4 seems like a very good idea. This stuff is so complex and is frequently not audited, I think it makes a lot of sense to require doc's here.

Regarding 13.3.3, shall we just say about application at all (as we could have something like middleware, etc.)?
For example:

13.3.3 Verify that all cryptographic operations are performed using an isolated security module (such as a vault or hardware security module) to securely manage and protect key material from exposure to **other application components**.

> Regarding 13.3.3, shall we just say about application at all (as we could have something like middleware, etc.)?
> For example:
> 
> 13.3.3 Verify that all cryptographic operations are performed using an isolated security module (such as a vault or hardware security module) to securely manage and protect key material from exposure to **other application components**.

I think this is an astute observation and it's a nice clean fix. I would suggest we are good to PR this one.

And for 13.3.2 @elarlang I keep going back and forth on this (as I often do). At one point it's just another authorization requirement. I see that perspective. 

But key management is special and becoming more common. If you get access control wrong at the key management level, it can be a rather high impact problem, like if you lose the signing key for JWT's. That's game over, man. Like from the movie "aliens". I would not complain if it went away, but if I had to vote I'd likely want to keep it in.
I removed 13.3.2 from the issue, issue description updated.
Colleagues, I only slightly changed wording, but if it reduces load to you, I can make PR.

> Colleagues, I only slightly changed wording, but if it reduces load to you, I can make PR.

I would suggest the following as slightly more accurate.:

13.3.3 Verify that all cryptographic operations are performed using an isolated security module (such as a vault or hardware security module) to securely manage and protect key material from exposure outside of the security module.

If you are comfortable with that then please open a PR @oleksiidov

@jmanico great clarification, really like it!
Will open a PR for 13.3.3.
